main_text.p: quæ passuum millia clxviii secundum Plinium in ambitu numerat. Tripolis erat ætate Homeri, urbes tum habens Lindum, Camirum, Ialysum, jam tum mari potens, sed sæculis posterioribus multò potentior. Tetrapolis demum facta est post Xerxem Persarum regem è Græcia profligatum, condita civitate nova, cui nomen totius insulæ datum: RHODVS scilicet vocata. Tradit Strabo, ferri vulgò, eundem architectum huic operi præfuisse, qui Piræi portum murumque construxit.

Insula tota optimè culta, tritici, vini, pomorum, aliorum fructuum feracissima, pecore omnis generis abundans, amæna undique, serenoque cœlo, præter urbes vicis & villis frequens, hic illic in montes aut colles se attollens, oblonga, ab austro in boream porrecta, colossô Solis vastæ molis, LXX cubitis à basi in altitudinem surgente, ex ære fusili celebris: quem colossum XII annorum labore Chares Lindius, juxta portum novæ urbis struxisse perhibetur, impendio publico talentorum CCC, inter septem mundi miracula computatum, sed annis LVI postquam erat absolutus, terræmotu prostratum, nec unquam postea rursus erectum.
Vrbs ipsa Rhodus commodo situ ad mare, paulatim è plan[?]

page.notes: The line "quæ passuum millia clxviii" is printed in small type; the numeral is copied as it appears. The catchword "quadam" at the lower right is partly faint and read with a doubt. The word ending the page, "plan", is broken at the line end; its continuation is in the catchword, so the hyphen-less break is marked [?]. Right margin marks near the last lines are too faint to read and are not transcribed. Left-edge strokes are show-through from the reverse and are omitted.
